- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), then undercorrects, leading to persistent overprediction.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values are rising sharply.
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- Lags in capturing sudden downward corrections — model reacts too slowly to price drops.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to account for volatility clustering or policy-driven price shocks.
- Forecasts often peak too early and then flatten, missing the true peak or subsequent rally.
- When true price exceeds forecast by >5%, model tends to overcorrect in next period, creating a “reversal” bias.
- Model underestimates price volatility in the final 10 days, leading to underprediction of sharp upward moves.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture abrupt changes in price direction or magnitude.
